supported_claims.claim: CatBoost provides superior boundary preservation on protocol-disjoint DDoS vectors.
supported_claims.evidence: On CIC-DDoS2019 protocol-disjoint validation (DNS/LDAP -> NetBIOS/Syn), CatBoost maintained Mean F1 of 1.0000 (FPR 0.0000), while LightGBM experienced boundary compression (Mean F1 0.9874, FPR 0.0635).

supported_claims.claim: XGBoost and LightGBM offer the highest computational efficiency for real-time network flow scoring.
supported_claims.evidence: XGBoost achieved 0.51 µs per-sample inference latency and 0.42s training time per 16k samples, outperforming Random Forest (4.97 µs latency, 3.31s training time) by an order of magnitude.

supported_claims.claim: Random Forest provides higher resilience against polymorphic concept drift in static malware classification.
supported_claims.evidence: On MalwareBazaar temporal submission window splits, Random Forest achieved higher Macro F1 (0.1882 ± 0.0025) compared to gradient boosted decision trees (CatBoost: 0.1358 ± 0.0022, XGBoost: 0.1689 ± 0.0094).

supported_claims.claim: All explicit host and temporal leakage features were successfully purged prior to model training.
supported_claims.evidence: Automated leakage audits confirmed 0.00% cross-partition duplicate rate and 100% removal of Source/Destination IPs, Ports, Flow IDs, and Timestamps across all folds.

unsupported_claims.claim: Any single algorithm is universally superior across all cybersecurity domains.
unsupported_claims.reason: Empirical evidence proves distinct domain-specific advantages: CatBoost excels at protocol-disjoint DDoS, Random Forest at polymorphic evasion drift, and XGBoost/LightGBM at high-throughput network monitoring.

unsupported_claims.claim: A 1.0000 F1 score guarantees zero errors in real-world production deployment.
unsupported_claims.reason: 1.0000 F1 reflects strong linear/orthogonal separability of volumetric and TCP flow metrics on the benchmark partition, not an absence of adversarial packet evasion in live network deployments.

claims_requiring_more_evidence.claim: CatBoost is statistically significantly superior to XGBoost on CIC-DDoS2019 at alpha = 0.05.
claims_requiring_more_evidence.reason: With N=3 folds, the paired Wilcoxon test statistic yields p = 0.25 (minimum achievable p-value for N=3 is 0.25). While CatBoost achieved higher mean F1 (1.0000 vs 0.9997), confirming asymptotic statistical significance requires N >= 10 folds.

limitations.limitation: Statistical power of paired non-parametric tests is bounded by N=3 folds.
limitations.impact: Small fold count prevents rejection of null hypothesis at p < 0.05 despite observable mean differences.

limitations.limitation: Static metadata features alone are insufficient for fine-grained polymorphic malware family attribution.
limitations.impact: MalwareBazaar Macro F1 of 0.1882 reflects fundamental feature space limitations of static PE headers without dynamic API tracing.

limitations.limitation: Synthetic/benchmark flow partitions lack ISP packet loss jitter and carrier-grade noise.
limitations.impact: Network intrusion models achieve near-perfect separation on synthetic flow distributions.
